title: MuViSU Retreat 2026
text:
Participant activity
Each participant should plan to bring a research activity to work on during the retreat, or be prepared to work with one or two other participants on their proposed activity. Think about what might be achieved in the 1.5 day time frame, and what might be an activity where getting input from others will be especially useful.

title: What to do before the retreat
text:
There is always more that we’d like to do that we have time for! The trick here is to map out one thing that would be useful to do for your work, likely achievable in the 1.5 day time frame.
It is also worthwhile to consider the opportunity to enage with others on this activity. If it is something that you don’t quite know how to achieve, but think that someone else’s expertise in the group might be able to get you over the line, this is possibly a wonderful activity to propose.
For example, students could focus on a particular section of their thesis, which might involve literature review, writing, an application or software development. Faculty might consider some part of their current work that would benefit from some dedicated time to develop, and insights from other faculty and students, which might be a part of a research project, application, blog post, or developing teaching materials.

Create an issue on the GitHub repo similar to the example, that briefly describes your planned activity.
Make sure you have the materials needed to complete your activity on your laptop, e.g. the most recent versions of R, and quarto or any other software needed.

title: Code of Conduct
text:
Code of Conduct
All participants are expected to be respectful, inclusive and welcoming, and to follow harassment-free behaviour standards throughout the retreat. Concerns can be raised with the organisers, who will address them promptly and confidentially.
